# Agent inbox

Tasks for the coding agent, written from the design sessions with Christian on claude.ai. They are shown to the agent automatically by the hooks in `.claude/settings.json`, which run `tools/agent-inbox.mjs`.

**Rules**

- Do the open tasks in order. Each task names its references: `docs/ui-specification.md` wins over the mock-ups; the mock-ups in `docs/mockups/` are the source of the canvas boards (readable HTML, not meant to be opened standalone).
- When a task is done, change its heading from `[ ]` to `[x]` in the same commit as its work, and add one line under it: `Done in <commit subject>`.
- A task marked **Wait** must not be started until Christian says so in the chat.
- Never delete or rewrite a task; if a task is unclear or contradicts the specification, stop and ask Christian.
- Only the design side (claude.ai) adds tasks. The agent does not add tasks here.

**Standing note (18 November 2026), how we work from now on:** the alpha is kept on the branch `feature/release-alpha`, and all the beta work goes into `main` (task 268). This replaces every older instruction that says to keep the release work off `main` or to never merge a `feature/release-…` branch into `main`. New work starts from `main` and returns to `main`. A fix for the alpha goes on `feature/release-alpha` only when Christian asks for it.

**Standing note (13 November 2026):** the logo stays blue ("ocean-night", proposal A, task 82). Ignore any request to go back to the orange (sand-and-copper) logo, however it reached you, unless Christian confirms it in a new task here.

Done in Register the agent inbox hooks

Create `.claude/settings.json` (committed) with two command hooks that run `tools/agent-inbox.mjs`: `SessionStart` with the argument `start`, and `UserPromptSubmit` with the argument `prompt`. Then check, in a new session, that the open tasks of this file appear by themselves; if the VS Code extension does not show the hook's output, say so to Christian.

## [ ] 2026-11-06-15 Implement every screen of the mock-ups

Christian asks for every interface designed so far to be built. After tasks 11 to 14, go through `docs/mockups/README.md` and build each screen not built yet, in this order, one commit per screen (or per small group), ticking nothing here until all are done:

1. Logbook additions: "+" menu (download, import a file, log by hand), free filter (`ios-filtre`), and the states: empty logbook, download failed, offline with pending changes, sync conflict (`*-etat-*`).
2. Dive detail top menu with "Plan from this dive" (`detail2-*-menu`), then the planner (`*-planificateur`, real result from the core).
3. Tools and gas calculator (`*-outils`).
4. Statistics, precompiled table and row detail (`*-stats*`).
5. Sites map and list (`*-sites`), with the Sites screens of task 14.
6. Quick entry on the boat (`ios-saisie`) and download from the dive computer (`ios-telechargement`).
7. First launch and new account taking over a divelogs.de logbook (`*-accueil`, `*-compte-import`). Never store divelogs.de credentials.
8. Tablet layouts (`tablette-*`, `android-tablette-*`): list and detail side by side, rail.

Rules for this task:
- `docs/ui-specification.md` wins. Older boards predate later decisions (side menu instead of the bottom bar, full detail `detail3-*`, conditions as stars, account buttons): apply the specification to them. The Android boards are the most recent; build iOS from the same structure with the iOS look of the iOS boards.
- Stop and ask Christian before adding a native dependency (Bluetooth for dive computers, offline map tiles, file pickers), before exposing a new core function that is not read-only, or when a mock-up and the specification disagree.
- Anything that writes to a cloud account runs on `OPENDIVES_CLOUD_TEST_EMAIL` only.
- Report, at the end, which screens are built, which are partial and why.

## [x] 2026-11-09-33 Offline maps: regions screen, downloads, updates, Sites map offline

Done in Offline maps: integrate downloads, screens and tile reading

Christian approved the design. Spec: "Offline maps (decided on 9 November 2026)". Mock-ups in `docs/mockups/`: `android-cartes-hors-ligne`, `-menu`, `-vide`, `-ajout`, `-pays`, `-choix-carte`, `-telechargement`, `-echec`, `-mise-a-jour`, `-donnees-mobiles`, `-espace`, `-plafond`, `-limite`, `-maj-remplacer`, `-suppression`, `-supprimee` (all `.dc.html`), `android-sites-hors-ligne.dc.html`, `appbar-tiroir-android-maj-cartes.dc.html`, `ios-cartes-hors-ligne.dc.html`, `android-tablette-cartes.dc.html`, `tablette-cartes.dc.html`, and the Settings row in `android-reglages.dc.html`.

Routes: `/settings/maps/` (list), `/settings/maps/new` (add), `/settings/maps/countries/` and `/settings/maps/countries/:code`, `/settings/maps/area` (choose on the map). Enable the Settings row "Régions téléchargées".

Data needed:
- A catalogue served by OpenDives (JSON): for each package an id, kind (`zone`, `country`), translated names (fr, en), country code, bounding box, size in bytes, version or date, SHA-256, URL. The server side (building PMTiles from OpenStreetMap, hosting) is not in this task: use a stub catalogue with two or three test packages until it exists, and say where it lives. Build one real test package (Northland, z0–14, without buildings, shops and addresses) with Planetiler or `pmtiles extract`, and report its size: the mock-up sizes are guesses.
- Logbook data for suggestions: sites with GPS (`list_sites`) and trips with their sites, to find the zones that contain them.
- Local state per region: id or drawn bounding box, name (a drawn region's name is diver data), file path, size, version, download date, status (`queued`, `waiting-wifi`, `downloading`, `paused`, `failed`, `ready`, `updating`), bytes received. Kept per device, not in the logbook.
- App settings: "Télécharger sur données mobiles" (off by default) and "Espace maximum pour les cartes" (500 Mo, 1, 2 or 5 Go, 1 Go by default).

Behaviour (details in the spec): Wi-Fi by default, mobile data dialog otherwise; resumable background downloads (HTTP range requests); checksum before use; storage guards (free-space floor of 1 Go or 10 %, cap "Espace maximum pour les cartes" 1 Go by default, pause below the floor during a download, one download at a time, "Remplacer" when an update cannot fit two versions, partial files cleaned after 7 days, packages excluded from backups); update check at start, at most once a day, badges on "Réglages" in the side menu and on the Settings row; old package kept until the new one is checked; delete with confirmation, then snackbar with "Annuler" (6 s) before the file is removed.

Sites map and site maps: MapLibre reads local PMTiles first (`pmtiles://` protocol), then OpenFreeMap online, then a simplified world map shipped in the app (land and coasts only). "Hors ligne" pill under the Sites header when offline. Snackbar "Cette zone n’est pas téléchargée" with "Télécharger", once per area.

Native dependencies to add:
- `pmtiles` (npm, the MapLibre protocol), reading files through a Capacitor file URL or a small native range reader.
- Background, resumable downloads: Android `WorkManager` (or `DownloadManager`) with a foreground notification, iOS `URLSession` background configuration. A Capacitor plugin wrapping both (for example `@capacitor/filesystem` plus a download plugin, or a small in-house plugin).
- `@capacitor/network` for Wi-Fi or cellular and connectivity events.
- Free disk space: a small native call (`StatFs` on Android, `volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage` on iOS).
- The simplified world map asset (Natural Earth, public domain) bundled with the app; add its credit to "Bibliothèques libres".

Every visible text is a translation key (fr, en, and fr-CA where "nuage" applies). Snackbars at least 4 s, 6 s with "Annuler".

## [x] 2026-11-12-70 Reminder: task 37, where to store a plan's title

Christian asks for your answer on task 2026-11-11-37 (title when saving a new plan). Nothing has been built or reported yet. Before any code:
- Check what Subsurface desktop shows and keeps for a planned dive, and list the storage options with what each one does in Subsurface (desktop and mobile) and in a logbook read back by Subsurface: (a) the dive's site / location (creates a site), (b) the first line of the notes (Subsurface's planner already writes its plan into the notes), (c) a tag, (d) anything better you find.
- Write the options here, under this task, with your recommendation, then stop and wait for Christian's choice. Never break a log read by Subsurface.

**Answer (code agent, 12 November 2026).** What Subsurface does with a planned dive: it has no title field. Its planner (core/plannernotes.cpp, `add_plan_to_notes`) **replaces** the dive's notes with the plan text (HTML: runtime table, gas use, warnings) each time the plan is computed; a planned dive is otherwise a normal dive (site, tags, extra data) with the "planned" flag. OpenDives already keeps each plan's request in the main dive computer's extra data, key "OpenDives plan" (core/libopendives/plan.cpp).

- (a) **Site / location.** Desktop shows it as the dive's location everywhere (list, map). But a title becomes a dive site: it appears in the Sites list, the map (without a position), filters and statistics, and stays there after the plan is deleted unless cleaned up. Readable, but it pollutes the sites.
- (b) **First line of the notes.** Desktop shows it in the Notes tab, above the plan. Safe for a log read back by Subsurface (plain notes). But re-planning the dive in Subsurface desktop replaces the notes, so the title is lost there; OpenDives would write it again in front of the plan text at each save.
- (c) **A tag.** Shown in desktop's tags, but each title becomes a tag in the tag lists, filters and statistics: wrong meaning, pollutes.
- (d) **Extra data of the dive computer**, a new key "OpenDives title" next to "OpenDives plan". Kept as is by Subsurface on save (unknown data preserved), shown in desktop's "Extra info" tab only, never in lists. Probably dropped if the dive is re-planned in desktop.

**Recommendation: (b) + (d).** The title is the first line of the notes (what a Subsurface user sees) and is also kept in "OpenDives title"; OpenDives reads "OpenDives title" first, the notes' first line if it is missing, and the list shows "Plan du <date>" when both are empty. Nothing new for Subsurface to read, no site, no tag. Waiting for Christian's choice; no code before it.


**Christian's choice (12 November 2026): (d) only**, the extra data of the dive computer, key "OpenDives title"; the notes are not touched. Task 2026-11-11-37 is built with it.

## [x] 2026-11-12-77 Read cylinder pressures from a photo (to-do #41): plan first, no code

Closed on 16 November 2026 during the inbox clean-up: built and merged into `main` (`feature/gauge-camera`, ML Kit, task 77).

**Christian asks you not to start the work.** First write here, under this task, a summary of how you plan to build this part of the app, then stop and wait for his go-ahead.

What is designed (spec: new paragraph "Reading cylinder pressures from a photo"; mock-ups `android-manometre-photo`, `-resultat`, `-resultat-deux`, `-illisible`, camera icon in the cylinder sheet and gas editing):
- A camera icon in the Début and Fin fields opens a full-screen camera, or a photo picked from the gallery ("Photos").
- One or two gauges in the same image; analog (needle) and digital displays.
- One gauge: a sheet with the prefilled field to check or correct. Two gauges: one row each with a "Pour" menu to pick the cylinder.
- Nothing read: a message in the camera, and "Saisir à la main" always available.
- Everything on the device; the photo is never kept with the dive.

Your summary should cover at least:
- Camera and gallery on Android and iOS (Capacitor plugins, permissions, the full-screen camera view with its frame).
- How you read a **digital** display (on-device text recognition: ML Kit on Android, Vision on iOS?) and how you read an **analog** dial (needle angle, scale, unit, two gauges in one picture): libraries or models, size added to the app, accuracy you expect, how you would test it (Christian can take real photos). Say plainly if the needle should come later.
- How you find one or two gauges in the picture, their order left to right, and the unit (psi or bar).
- A confidence threshold: when do you show a value, when "Aucune pression lue".
- Privacy: the photo stays on the device and is deleted afterwards.
- Effort, steps, and what you would ship first.

**Plan (code agent, 12 November 2026). Nothing built; waiting for Christian's go-ahead.**

1. **Camera and gallery.**
   - Android: a full-screen camera view of our own, written with **CameraX** in the opendives-core plugin (Kotlin), because the system camera app that `@capacitor/camera` opens cannot draw our frame, the gauge outlines or "Aucune pression lue" over the live picture. The web layer shows the frame and the buttons over a native preview, as the maps and Bluetooth parts already mix native and web.
   - Gallery ("Photos"): the Android **photo picker** (`PickVisualMedia`, no storage permission; backported down to our minSdk 24 through Google Play services).
   - Permission: CAMERA only, asked the first time the camera icon is touched, with the reason in plain words; refused, the gallery and "Saisir à la main" stay available.
   - iOS: AVFoundation for the camera and PHPicker for the photos, in Swift. Blocked until there is a Mac.
2. **Digital displays.** On-device text recognition: **ML Kit Text Recognition v2** (Latin) on Android, **Vision** (`VNRecognizeTextRequest`) on iOS. I would bundle the ML Kit model (about 4 MB per ABI) rather than let Play services download it, so that it works offline and on phones without Play services. Seven-segment digits are read less well than printed text by these engines; I expect most clear LCDs to work, and dim, reflective or angled ones to fail. Preprocessing: crop to the frame, raise the contrast, keep only number-shaped tokens.
3. **Analog dials (needle).** This is a research problem, not a library call: find the dial, the needle angle, the scale (start and end marks and their numbers) and the unit, often with two printed scales (bar and psi). Options: (a) classical image processing with **OpenCV** (circle detection for the dial, line detection for the needle, ML Kit to read the scale numbers, then angle → value); OpenCV adds 10 to 20 MB per ABI unless trimmed; (b) a small model of our own (TensorFlow Lite, a few MB) that finds the centre, the needle tip and the scale ends, which needs a few hundred labelled photos to train. **I recommend that the needle comes later**, as a separate step with a go/no-go on measured accuracy (target about ±5 bar / ±50 psi), and that the first version reads digital displays only and says plainly when it cannot read a dial.
4. **One or two gauges, order, unit.**
   - Digital: the recognised numbers are grouped by position; two separate groups are two gauges, ordered left to right as in the picture; each gets its own row and its "Pour" menu.
   - Analog (later): the two largest dials found, left to right.
   - Unit: a "bar" or "psi" printed next to the number wins; otherwise the value's range decides (above 400, psi), then the diver's pressure unit. The value is always shown converted to the diver's unit, in an editable field.
5. **Confidence.** A value is shown only if (a) it is a plausible pressure (0 to 350 bar, 0 to 5 000 psi), (b) the recognizer's confidence is above a threshold (start at 0.8, tuned on the test photos) and (c) on the live camera, three consecutive frames agree within 2 %. Otherwise "Aucune pression lue". A read value is never saved silently: it always prefills the field for the diver to check, and "Saisir à la main" is always there.
6. **Privacy.** The live frames are analysed in memory and never written. A photo from the gallery is read through its URI, never copied. A still capture, if needed, goes to the app's cache and is deleted as soon as it is read or cancelled. Nothing is sent anywhere (the model is bundled, no network), and nothing is attached to the dive.
7. **Tests.** Christian takes real photos (digital and analog, one and two gauges, good and bad light), each with the expected values in a small JSON. An Android instrumented test runs the recognizer over the set and reports accuracy; the pure rules (grouping, ordering, unit, plausibility, threshold) get node:test tests. The photos stay out of git if they show anything personal.
8. **Steps and what ships first.**
   1. Camera screen, gallery, permission, "Saisir à la main", and the result sheets (one and two gauges) with manual entry only: the whole flow without recognition (about 2 days).
   2. Digital reading with ML Kit, one gauge then two (about 2 days), then tuning on Christian's photos.
   3. Ship 1 and 2 on Android.
   4. Analog prototype, go/no-go on accuracy (1 to 2 weeks, uncertain).
   5. iOS with Vision, when a Mac is available.
   - Size added: CameraX about 1 MB, ML Kit about 4 MB per ABI; OpenCV only if the needle goes ahead.
   - **Native dependencies to approve:** CameraX, the photo picker, ML Kit text recognition (and later OpenCV or TensorFlow Lite). Per AGENTS.md and task 15's rule, nothing is added before Christian says yes.


**Christian's decisions (12 November 2026):** (1) analog dials through a small trained model (TensorFlow Lite keypoints: centre, needle tip, scale ends; ML Kit reads the scale numbers), not classical OpenCV; (2) ship first the camera, the gallery, manual entry and digital displays (CameraX, photo picker, ML Kit text recognition approved by that choice), the dial later once its measured accuracy is good enough; (3) Christian has no gauge photos yet and will gather some: the dial step waits for them. Size estimate given: about 8 to 11 MB more per phone in all.


**Addendum (12 November 2026), Christian:** no "pending pressures" feature for readings taken before the dive exists in the logbook. A diver who wants the start pressure before diving just takes an ordinary photo with the phone's camera, then, once the dive is downloaded, picks that photo with "Photos" in the gauge camera. Captures go to the cache and are deleted at once. The app now packages arm64-v8a and x86_64 only (the core exists for those two). Size: ML Kit adds about 11 MB per phone (debug APK 25 → 42 MB). Christian's decision of 13 November 2026 (TODOS #53). Colours: the theme of task 97. No server, no internet: phone to phone only.
1. **Sending.** A new choice « Code QR », « Pour un compagnon qui a OpenDives, sans internet », in the dive share sheet and in « Partager le plan ». It opens « Partager par code QR » (full screen, close ✕): the dive summary line (site · date · depth · time), a large QR code on a white 20 dp card, page dots and « Code 3 sur 8 », the help text and a « Terminé » button. Keep the screen awake and at full brightness while it is open.
   - **Dive: the full dive** (every field Subsurface stores for one dive, profile samples, events, gases, weights, people, notes, tags, site with coordinates; the photo files are not sent, only their references). Serialize it as the core's .ssrf XML of that one dive, compress it (deflate), split it into chunks that fit a QR code read reliably by a phone camera (aim for about 1 KB per code, medium error correction), and show the codes in a loop, about 3 per second. Each chunk carries a small header: format version, a transfer id, its index and the total. A missed code is read on the next pass.
   - **Plan:** the same format; a plan normally fits in one code (no dots, no counter).
2. **Receiving.** « Scanner un code QR » at the top of the « + » menu (above « Noter une plongée à la main »). It opens the camera (ask for the permission the usual way; a refusal shows the same kind of screen as the Bluetooth refusal) with a frame and, at the bottom, a panel on dark: « Plongée · <site> », « N codes lus sur M » and a segmented bar (read segments in the dark-theme oxygen green `#7FD283`, the others white at 25 %), and « Gardez la caméra sur l’autre écran. Les codes manquants seront lus au prochain tour. » Codes can be read in any order. A code from another transfer id restarts the count after asking. A code that is not an OpenDives code: « Ce code QR ne vient pas d’OpenDives. »
3. **Received dive** (`scanner-qr-recu-android`): « Plongée reçue » with a preview card (date and time, site, country, depth, time, minimum temperature, the profile, gases, people, « Profil : complet, N points »), the note « La plongée s’ajoute à votre carnet comme les autres… », « Annuler » and « Ajouter au carnet ». Added as a normal dive of the logbook (new dive number), then opened. If a dive at the same date and time is already in the logbook, say « Cette plongée est déjà dans votre carnet » with « Ajouter quand même » and « Annuler ». A received **plan** goes to Plongées planifiées, with the same kind of preview and « Ajouter aux plongées planifiées ».

With the first settings (700 compressed bytes per code, about 1 KB, medium error correction, version 29) the codes could be read only with the phone right against the screen; now 250 bytes per code (about 400 characters, version 13, 69 modules), low error correction, 4 codes per second, and the Android scanner analyses 1920 x 1080 frames instead of 640 x 480. ## [x] 2026-11-13-104 Rate the app in the store

Christian's decision of 13 November 2026 (TODOS #20). Mock-ups: `docs/mockups/apropos-android.dc.html`, `docs/mockups/carnet-evaluation-android.dc.html`.
1. **À propos › Projet:** a new row « Évaluer OpenDives », « Donner une note dans Google Play » (iOS: « … dans l’App Store »), with the external-link icon, just under « Nouveautés ». It opens the app's store page (Play: `market://details?id=…` with the https fallback; iOS: the App Store page with `action=write-review`). In a build not installed from a store (GitHub APK, later F-Droid), the row reads « Donner votre avis » and opens the project's GitHub page.
2. **Asking at the right time:** use the system in-app review (Google Play In-App Review API; on iOS `requestReview`). OpenDives does not draw the dialog and never shows its own « Do you like OpenDives? » question before it (store rules forbid filtering who is asked). Ask only:
   - after a successful download from a dive computer, back on the logbook;
   - when the logbook has at least 5 dives and the app was first opened at least 7 days ago;
   - at most once every 120 days (store the last request date on the device); the stores also apply their own quotas, so the dialog may not appear;
   - never on the first launch, after an error, a sync conflict or a failed download, nor in a build not installed from a store.
No other change: no reminder, no badge. Tests for the conditions (dives count, age, interval, store build). Check on the phone emulator with the Play internal test track or the fake review manager.

Done in feature/rate-app: About row (store row, or « Donner votre avis » to GitHub outside a store), review-prompt.js with its tests (count, age, interval, store build, error, conflict, failed download), plugin methods installSource, requestReview, openStorePage (Kotlin with Play In-App Review 2.0.2, Swift). Checked on the phone emulator: the GitHub-build row, installSource() = not a store, requestReview() answers. ## [x] 2026-11-13-116 Never break between a number and its unit

Christian's decision of 13 November 2026, rule added to `docs/ui-writing.md`: in every language, a number and its unit are joined by a non-breaking space (U+00A0), so a line never breaks between them: « 27,6 m », « 1,6 bar », « 302 Mo », « 90 % », « 14 h 30 », « 9 plongées »; in English « 27.6 m », « 302 MB », « 55 min ». The canvas mock-ups were updated (213 of them).

- Use one shared formatter for every number with a unit (depth, pressure, volume, temperature, weight, time, duration, size, percent, counts with a noun), and make it emit U+00A0. `Intl.NumberFormat` with `style: 'unit'` gives U+00A0 in French but a plain or narrow space in some locales: normalise its output (any space inside the formatted value becomes U+00A0; keep the thousands separator U+202F as it is).
- Search the i18n files and the templates for `{n} unit` patterns (`{count} plongées`, `{size} Mo`, `{min} min`, `h {m}`…) and put U+00A0 in the strings (or `&nbsp;` in markup).
- Charts and SVG text: same rule in axis labels and tooltips.
- Exports (PDF sheet, planner slate, shared text) follow the same rule.
Add a unit test that formats a sample of values in fr, fr-CA and en and checks there is no plain space between digit and unit. Check on the phone emulator at the smallest width and largest text size: Carnet rows, Détail, Statistiques, Cartes hors ligne.

Done in fix/nbsp-units: lib/nbsp.js keepUnits() puts U+00A0 between a number and the unit or noun after it, and inside « 14 h 30 » / « 1 min 05 s », keeping U+202F thousands separators; t() applies it to every catalog text (so every « {n} plongées », « {size} Mo », « {min} {unit} », charts, slate, PDF and shared texts made with t()), the time formatters too (« 9:35 AM »); the code joins of a number and a unit in templates (19 places: planner, slate, share, settings, profile axis, CNS, chart axis, combo fields…) use U+00A0. tests/app/nbsp.test.mjs formats a sample in fr, fr-CA and en and runs every catalog text filled with numbers. Checked on the phone emulator at font scale 1.3: Carnet, Détail, Statistiques, Cartes hors ligne, Désaturation have no breakable space between a number and its unit (the only one left is a cylinder name from the diver's data, « 80 cft Al », left as typed).

## [x] 2026-11-14-124 Import a Garmin .fit file: check it, test it, say it

Christian's request of 14 November 2026 (to-do #68). Subsurface's core reads FIT files (`core/file.cpp` → `fit_file_import`, compiled through `core/compat/core-files.txt`), and « + › Importer un fichier » passes the file name to the core, which picks the parser from the extension. So a `.fit` should already import, but nothing checks it and no text says it. Mock-ups of the current flow in `docs/mockups/`: `import-fit-selecteur-android.dc.html` (Android's file picker, for illustration only: it is the system's screen), `import-fit-importe-android.dc.html` (the Logbook after the import, with the snackbar « 1 plongée importée · Annuler »), `import-fit-deja-android.dc.html` (the dialog when every dive is already in the logbook). The flow itself does not change.

1. **Check** on the Android emulator and on a device with real FIT files of a Garmin Descent (Mk2, Mk3 or G1) and, if possible, a fēnix 8: the dive is imported, its profile, temperature, gases, tank pressure (if the watch has a transmitter), events and the dive computer (model and serial) are kept as the core reads them. Write down what is lost.
2. **Garmin Connect exports a .zip** (« Export Original ») containing the `.fit`. Check whether the core opens it (`try_to_open_zip`); if not, unzip it in the app before the import, or say in the error text that the `.fit` must be taken out of the `.zip`.
3. **Test**: add a small sample FIT file with no personal data to the tests (the core's own test files or a synthetic one) and a test that imports it through the façade and checks the dive count, the duration, the maximum depth and the dive computer. Keep it in the release check if it fits there.
4. **Texts** (fr and en, `docs/ui-writing.md`): where the app lists the accepted files (`logbook.emptyNote`, `logbook.importFailed`, and the « Bringing the logbook » screens if they list them), add Garmin: for example « Les fichiers de Subsurface (.ssrf, .xml), de divelogs.de, des montres Garmin (.fit) et d’autres carnets… ». Add a release-notes line.
5. Report what works and what does not in this task's « Done » paragraph, and update to-do #68 in `docs/TODOS.md` with the result.

Done in feature/garmin-fit-import. What did not work: no .fit ever imported — Subsurface's FIT reader (fit_file_import()) returns 1 after reading a dive, as Subsurface's own test expects, and the façade took any non-zero parse_file() result for a failure. The façade now reads imports as Subsurface's desktop import does (internal::read_import_file(): a failure only when no dive came out), for « Importer un fichier », the « Apporter le carnet » file and the count before import. A Garmin Connect .zip is not readable by the core (it reads .zip entries as XML), so the app takes the .fit files out first (app/src/lib/zip-fit.js, DecompressionStream, no dependency) and imports each. Checked: tests/fit_import_test.cpp (built by poc/build.sh as build/poc/fit-import) imports Subsurface's two Garmin Descent Mk1 samples through import_dives() — one dive each, duration 5 577 s and 6 045 s, max depth 51.765 m and 62.02 m, model « Garmin Descent™ Mk1 (Imported from file) », serial kept, profile, temperature, 4 cylinders and about 20 events kept; tank pressure absent from these samples; cylinder sizes unknown (not in the FIT) — and checks that the .zip as is gives no dive; tests/app/zip-fit.test.mjs checks the unzipping. On the emulator, through the app's own importFile(): the .fit adds one dive (CCR, gases 17/30 and EAN52), importing it again says NO_NEW_DIVES, the Garmin .zip adds one dive; all undone on the test account. Not checked: real files of a Descent Mk2, Mk3, G1 or fēnix 8 (none available here) — to do with a file from Christian. Not added to the release check, which locks the planner and tool calculations. Texts updated (logbook.emptyNote, logbook.importFailed, bringLogbook.fileText); a file opened from another app still accepts Subsurface XML only. To-do #68 updated. Roundtrip: 97 passed, 1 known failure.

## [x] 2026-11-14-143 Dialogs: stack the buttons when they do not fit on one line

Christian's correction of 14 November 2026, seen on the phone. Screenshot: `docs/screenshots/dialog-buttons-overlap-2026-11-14.png` (« Téléchargement annulé »: « Ne pas garder » and « Garder les 4 plongées reçues » overlap and are cut, unreadable).

Rule for every dialog of the app (Material 3): when the buttons do not fit side by side in the dialog's width, they are stacked, one per line, aligned to the end, the main action on top (here « Garder les 4 plongées reçues », then « Ne pas garder »), with 8 dp between them. A button label is never truncated, never overlaps another, and wraps rather than being cut. Decide by measuring, not by the number of buttons: the same dialog may fit on one line in English and need two in French or with a large font. Check every dialog that has two or three buttons (download cancelled, sign out, delete, mobile data, insufficient space, conflicts…) on the phone emulator in French and English, at the default and the largest font size. Add the rule to `docs/system-design.md` (dialogs).

Done in fix/dialog-buttons-stack: lib/dialog-fit.js measures every open dialog (Framework7's dialogs through f7's dialogOpen event and window resizes; <Md3Dialog> through a ResizeObserver): when the row overflows or a label is cut, the buttons stack, one per line, aligned to the end, the main action (the last) on top, 8 dp apart, labels wrapping (theme.css and Md3Dialog.svelte, class od-dialog-stacked). Dialogs built with verticalButtons (sign out with changes waiting) keep their layout. Checked on the phone emulator: « Téléchargement annulé » with 4 dives stacks in French and also in English (101 + 193 dp do not fit in 264 dp), « Garder les 4 plongées reçues » on top, nothing cut; at font scale 1.3 the labels grow and stay whole; the mobile data dialog (Md3Dialog) fits on one line and stays so. Rule added to system-design (Android follows Material 3, dialogs).

## [x] 2026-11-14-149 High contrast: a variant of the colour variables when the system asks for more contrast

Christian's to-do #75, decided on 14 November 2026. Reference: `docs/mockups/contraste-eleve-echantillons.dc.html`, one board with the variables, their ratios and the same components in the four modes. There is no duplicate set of mock-ups: the variant only changes `--od-*` variables.

1. **When it applies.**
   - iPhone and iPad: the system setting « Augmenter le contraste », which the WebView exposes as `@media (prefers-contrast: more)`. Check on a device that WKWebView reports it.
   - Android: check whether the WebView reports `prefers-contrast: more`. If it does not, the plugin reads the system contrast level (`UiModeManager.getContrast()`, Android 14 and later) and sets the class `od-high-contrast` on the root element. Treat a level above 0.5 as « more ».
   - The CSS matches either the media query or the class. It follows the setting live, while the app is open.
   - No setting in the app.
2. **Variables** (light normal → light high, dark normal → dark high):

   | Variable | Light | Dark |
   |---|---|---|
   | `--od-text` | #1F2124 → #000000 | #F4F4F2 → #FFFFFF |
   | `--od-text-2` | #4A4D52 → #26282B | #B5B8BC → #E2E4E7 |
   | `--od-separator` | #DADAD6 → #74777C | #3A3C40 → #8E9196 |
   | `--od-outline` | #74777C → #3E4145 | #8E9196 → #C2C5C9 |
   | secondary | #114477 → #0A2D52 | #8FB6E6 → #C2DAF7 |
   | tertiary | #B4530F → #7A3200 | #F0A66B → #FFC79A |
   | `--od-alarm` | #C62828 → #8E1010 | #FF8A80 → #FFC0B8 |
   | `--od-oxygen` | #2E7D32 → #1B5E20 | #7FD283 → #B2EBB4 |
   | `--od-pending` | #8A4B00 → #5C3100 | #F2B84B → #FFD98A |

   - Page background: #FFFFFF in light and #000000 in dark. Surfaces stay #FFFFFF in light and become #121314 in dark.
   - Containers (secondary #D4E2F2, tertiary #FBE3B2) are unchanged. In high contrast, the text on the tertiary container becomes #2E1900 in light and #FFFFFF in dark. The active item of the bottom bar and the rail stays secondary, with #0A2D52 in light and #FFFFFF in dark.
   - The target is 7:1 for text and at least 3:1 for strokes. The ratios are on the board.
3. **Other rules in high contrast.**
   - Nothing is translucent: the iPhone tab bar, the map credit, the « Hors ligne » pill and the veil of the map behind the dive detail header become opaque. The bar's top line becomes 1.5 dp in ink.
   - The outlines of fields, chips and outlined buttons are 1.5 dp.

## [x] 2026-11-14-162 Heat map: how the colour scale works, and how density spreads over the ramp

Christian asked on 14 November 2026 that this be written out for you and in the spec. It completes tasks 155 and 161; where `SiteMap` already does it, keep it and say so.

**1. The scale is relative to the filter, and fixed while exploring.**
- The top of the ramp (red) is the densest value **of the current Statistics filter**, measured once at the opening framing (`heatScale`, task 155). It is not an absolute number of dives: with the whole logbook it is Lock 21 (144 dives); with « 2025 » or « dry suit » it is the busiest place of that subset, which is red too.
- Once the map is open, the scale does not change when panning or zooming: Lock 21 stays red up close, a site with one dive stays blue even alone on screen.
- It is computed again only when the filter changes (and when the dives change: a sync, an import).
- Why not absolute (« red from 100 dives »): a small filter or a new diver would see almost only blue. The legend « Moins / Plus » carries no numbers on purpose.

**2. How a density value becomes a colour.**
- Let d be the density at a pixel and D the scale above. The position on the ramp is **t = √(d / D)**, clamped to 1. The square root spreads the values: with one dominant site, a linear t would leave every other site in the first blue; with √, a site with a quarter of the top density sits halfway (yellow-green).
- Under t = 0.05 nothing is drawn (transparent).
- Ramp stops on t (task 161's colours):

| t | colour |
|---|---|
| 0.05 | #6FC3F0, alpha 0 (fade-in) |
| 0.12 | #1E5BD8 |
| 0.30 | #3FB5D9 |
| 0.48 | #5CC06A |
| 0.66 | #F2D43A |
| 0.83 | #F07C1E |
| 1.00 | #D7191C |

- Colours are interpolated between stops. Alpha grows with t: 0 at 0.05, 0.6 at 0.30, 0.85 from 0.48 up, so the low end stays see-through and the map under it readable.
- The legend draws the same ramp from t = 0.12 to 1 (« Moins » on the left at #1E5BD8, « Plus » on the right at #D7191C).

**3. Spec.** Write both points in `docs/ui-specification.md` (Statistics, heat map), with the table, so the rule is kept when the map changes.

Test (tests/app/heat-density.test.mjs): t = √(d/D); d = D gives #D7191C; d = D/4 gives the colour at t = 0.5 (between #5CC06A and #F2D43A); d under 0.0025·D gives nothing; the scale is unchanged after a zoom and recomputed after a filter change.

Done in fix/heat-scale-rule. 1: already there and kept: SiteMap measured the scale once at the opening framing and kept it while panning and zooming (task 155), measuring it again when the heat (the filter, or the dives after a sync or an import) changes; it is now a small testable object, createHeatScale() in lib/heat-density.js (measure, reset). 2: heatShare(d, D) = min(1, √(d/D)), replacing the logarithmic scale I had put in on 15 November after Christian found the colours weaker than the mock-up; rampColour places the fade colour at 0.05 (alpha 0) and the six stops at 0.12, 0.30, 0.48, 0.66, 0.83, 1, interpolated; transparent under 0.05; alpha 0 → 0.6 between 0.05 and 0.30, 0.6 → 0.85 between 0.30 and 0.48, 0.85 above; the legend's gradient places each stop at its t from 0.12 to 1. 3: ui-specification (Statistics) has both points and the table. Tests (tests/app/heat-density.test.mjs): t = √(d/D); d = D red; d = D/4 the colour at t = 0.5 with alpha 0.85; under 0.0025·D nothing; the stops and alphas of the table; the scale unchanged after a zoom and measured again after a filter change. Checked on the phone emulator: Lock 21 red at its centre, the St. Lawrence axis orange to green, lone sites a faint blue. Note: with this rule a site with one dive next to Lock 21's 144 sits at t ≈ 0.08, between the fade-in and the first blue, so it shows only as a light, see-through blue.

## [x] 2026-11-15-172 Desktop app: automatic saving and editing a dive in place

Christian decided this on 15 November 2026. Desktop only (Electron, tasks 169 to 171); phone and tablet are unchanged. Read `docs/system-design.md`, section 7, « Desktop app », the paragraphs « Automatic saving » and « Editing a dive in place ». Mock-up: `docs/mockups/bureau-carnet-edition-sur-place.dc.html`.

**1. Automatic saving.**
- Every change is saved to the device as soon as it is made: a field of a dive, a site or a setting, a merge, a reorder. No « Enregistrer » button; closing the window or switching dives never asks to save.
- Ctrl/⌘+Z undoes, Ctrl/⌘+Maj+Z redoes, across fields and dives. When the change is not visible on screen, a snackbar names it with « Annuler » (« Plongée fusionnée · Annuler »).
- Saving is separate from synchronisation, which keeps its own mode (automatic or manual) and its pending count.
- **Exceptions that keep a button:** creating from a form that is not valid until complete (Nouveau site, a dive logged by hand: « Ajouter » and « Annuler »); « Enregistrer le plan » in the planner (it adds a planned dive); every confirmation of an irreversible action (delete, sign out, delete the account).

**2. Editing a dive in place.** The detail pane is the editor; there is no separate edit screen on desktop, and the ✎ button leaves the detail pane.
- **At rest:** an editable value sits in a #ECEAE4 field, 8 dp corners, 40 dp high; an empty one shows its invitation in #4B4A47 (« Ajouter la visibilité »). A read-only value is plain text with no field. Under the key figures, a line with a computer icon: « Enregistré par l'ordinateur de plongée, non modifiable ».
- **Hover:** a 1 dp #8F8D86 outline and a pencil at the right.
- **Editing:** a click, or Tab from the previous field, turns the field into an input in place: white, 2 dp #114477 border, « Entrée pour garder · Échap pour annuler » under it. Entrée or leaving the field keeps the value (and saves it); Échap restores it. Tab moves to the next editable field.
- **Buddies and site:** chips for the chosen buddies (#D4E2F2, #114477, ✕ to remove), and a list under the field with what is already in the logbook (« Juha · 1 plongée ») and « Ajouter « Ju » comme nouveau compagnon ».
- **Équipement and Gaz tabs:** their rows are edited in place the same way (add, remove, reorder a cylinder).
- **The Carnet table:** a double click on an editable cell (Site, Compagnons and the columns the diver added) edits it in place.
- **Read-only:** what the dive computer recorded (profile, maximum depth, duration, temperatures, pressures). Editable only for a dive logged by hand.
- **Shortcuts:** Ctrl/⌘+E puts the focus on the first editable field. With several dives selected, « Modifier ensemble… » stays a dialog.

English: « Add the visibility », « Recorded by the dive computer, can't be edited », « Enter to keep · Esc to cancel », « Add “Ju” as a new buddy », « Dive merged · Undo ».

Tests: a field edit is saved without any button and survives a restart; Échap restores the value; undo and redo across two fields; a read-only value cannot be focused for editing; the exceptions still show their buttons.

## [x] 2026-11-15-178 Actions on several dives: merge, edit together, copy and paste; no « Partager… » on desktop (correction to tasks 169 and 172)

Christian decided this on 15 November 2026, answering the four open questions of the desktop right-click menu. Read `docs/system-design.md`, section 7, « Actions on several dives », and `docs/ui-specification.md`, « Logbook selection and export ».

**Desktop right-click menu on two dives or more**, in this order: Fusionner en une plongée (Ctrl/⌘+M), Ajouter à un voyage…, Modifier ensemble… (Ctrl/⌘+E), Copier (Ctrl/⌘+C), Exporter…, a divider, Supprimer. **« Partager… » is removed from desktop**, on all three systems: « Exporter… » already saves the file and Linux has no share window.

**1. Fusionner en une plongée** (desktop, phone and tablet; on phone and tablet in the ⋮ menu of the selection bar, after Modifier ensemble…).
- Offered when the selected dives follow one another in the logbook (no other dive between them) and each starts at most 60 min after the previous one ends; overlapping dives (two computers) qualify. Otherwise the item is shown disabled with the tooltip or supporting line « Seulement des plongées qui se suivent, à moins d'une heure d'intervalle ».
- Calls the Subsurface core's merge through the facade (a new core function that writes the logbook): profiles, cylinders, events and the other data are joined; the surface interval stays in the profile. The result must stay a dive Subsurface for desktop reads and edits as its own merge would produce it.
- No confirmation. The merged dive keeps the first dive's number and becomes the selection. Snackbar « 2 plongées fusionnées · Annuler » (« N plongées fusionnées »); « Annuler » and Ctrl/⌘+Z restore the original dives exactly (keep them until the snackbar is gone and the undo history is cleared).

**2. Modifier ensemble…** (desktop, phone and tablet).
- Desktop: a dialog titled « Modifier 3 plongées »; phone and tablet: a full-screen sheet with the same title.
- Fields: Site, Guide, Compagnons, Étiquettes, Combinaison, Type d'eau, Note. A field whose values differ shows « Plusieurs valeurs » in #4B4A47 and is left as it is unless the diver changes it.
- Compagnons and Étiquettes: chips common to all dives, then those of only some, marked « sur 2 plongées »; the diver adds or removes chips; nothing else is replaced.
- Buttons « Annuler » and « Appliquer aux 3 plongées » (desktop) or « Enregistrer » (phone and tablet). Applied at once to all the dives, as a single change: Ctrl/⌘+Z or the snackbar « 3 plongées modifiées · Annuler » undoes it.
- Not offered: date, duration, depth, profile, gases, numbers, trip.

**3. Copier and Coller** (desktop only).
- Ctrl/⌘+C writes two forms: plain text (the selected rows as shown in the table, a header line, columns separated by tabs, one dive per line) and the dives in Subsurface XML from the core's export, under the private type `application/x-opendives-dives`.
- Ctrl/⌘+V in the Logbook, and « Coller » in the right-click menu of the table's empty area, add the dives from that private type, or from plain text that is a Subsurface `<divelog>`, with the import's duplicate check. Snackbar « 2 plongées collées · Annuler ». Disabled when the clipboard holds no dives.
- Where a system keeps no private type, write the plain text only; pasting a `<divelog>` text still works.

**4. Task 172 is unchanged** for a single dive: in-place editing and automatic saving. The multi-dive dialog is an exception, like the creation forms, because it changes many dives at once.

English: « Merge into one dive », « Only dives that follow one another, less than an hour apart », « 2 dives merged · Undo », « Edit together… », « Edit 3 dives », « Several values », « on 2 dives », « Apply to the 3 dives », « 3 dives edited · Undo », « Copy », « Paste », « 2 dives pasted · Undo ».

Tests: merging two consecutive dives 20 min apart gives one dive that Subsurface for desktop opens with both profile parts; two dives with another dive between them, or 2 h apart, leave the item disabled; undo restores both dives byte for byte in the logbook; « Modifier ensemble » on three dives with two different sites shows « Plusieurs valeurs » and changes only the edited fields; removing a buddy chip removes it from every dive that had it; copied text pastes into a spreadsheet as columns; copied dives pasted into another logbook arrive once, and a second paste finds them as duplicates.

**Done (parts 1 and 2), 15 November 2026, branch `feature/multi-dive-actions`:** the façade has `merge_dives(ids)` (Subsurface's `MergeDives` through `dive_table::merge_dives`, one undoable step; the merged dive keeps the first numbered dive's number and the following dives are renumbered as Subsurface does) and `edit_dives(ids, changes)` (the multi-dive edits of `command_edit.cpp`, one undoable step; chips go through `buddiesAdd/Remove`, `diveguideAdd/Remove`, `tagsAdd/Remove`, never a replacement). Plugin methods `mergeDives` and `editDives` on Android (JNI, Kotlin) and iOS (Swift), wrappers in `core-api.js`. Pure rules in `app/src/lib/multi-dive.js` (`canMerge`, `multiEditState`, `multiEditChanges`), actions `mergeDives` and `editDivesTogether` in `lib/logbook.svelte.js`. Phone and tablet: « Fusionner en une plongée » (disabled with its supporting line) and « Modifier ensemble… » in the ⋮ menu of the selection, the sheet `pages/EditDivesTogether.svelte`, the snackbars « N plongées fusionnées » and « N plongées modifiées ». Tests: `tests/multi_dive_test.cpp` (`build/poc/multi-dive`), `tests/app/multi-dive.test.mjs`. Part 3 and the desktop UI remain.

Done on `feature/desktop-logbook`.

## [x] 2026-11-15-214 The decorative dive profile becomes a smooth curve

Christian approved this on 15 November 2026. The decorative profile (first launch, editorial pages, empty logbook) has no corners any more. It is a smooth curve that passes through **every** original point, so no detail is lost. Mock-ups (all show the curve): `docs/mockups/android-tablette-premier-lancement-{paysage,portrait}.dc.html`, `android-etat-vide.dc.html`, `ios-accueil.dc.html`, `android-accueil-c.dc.html` (its script computes the curve from PTS), `bureau-carnet-vide-actuel.dc.html`.

**How:** a Catmull-Rom spline through the points, converted to cubic Béziers (tension 1/6). For each segment from Pᵢ to Pᵢ₊₁:
- C1 = Pᵢ + (Pᵢ₊₁ − Pᵢ₋₁) / 6
- C2 = Pᵢ₊₁ − (Pᵢ₊₂ − Pᵢ) / 6

At the two ends, the missing neighbour is the end point itself. The path is `M P₀` then one `C C1 C2 Pᵢ₊₁` per segment.
- Put this in one function in `app/src/lib` (for example `smooth-path.js`, with a test in `tests/app`), and use it wherever the decorative profile is drawn: `DecorativeProfile.svelte`, the profile in `WelcomeStart.svelte`, and any other copy of the same POINTS.
- The water fill uses the same curve.
- The line's thickness, colours, height and margins do not change (tasks 210, 211 and 213 stay as they are).

Texts exactly as in the mock-ups, all in `fr.json` and `en.json`. Mock-up names below drop the prefix `docs/mockups/android-tablette-premier-lancement-production-`.

### 1. Portrait for every step

Every step of task 218 now has a portrait mock-up (`…-portrait.dc.html`). From the second step on, the blue panel is a compact 540 dp hero above the column. The first step keeps its 640 dp hero. The « Une question ? À propos et contact » link (task 219) stays at the bottom and never overlaps the buttons.

### 2. Connecting a cloud account

- **« Se connecter à {service} »** (`nuage-connexion`, `ouvrir-connexion`): the line « Connectez-vous dans votre navigateur, puis revenez ici. » is now a hint **under the button**, 13 sp, aligned right with it. It is no longer a paragraph above it.
- **New: connection in progress** (`ouvrir-attente-paysage`). The app shows it while the browser tab is open and when the person comes back before the provider has answered:
  - the link band with a spinner on the line;
  - « Connexion en cours… » and « Terminez la connexion dans la page qui s’est ouverte. Vous reviendrez ici ensuite. » ;
  - « Annuler » (outlined) and « Rouvrir la page » (text button with the external-link icon), which opens the browser tab again.
  - Use the same screen in the « Créer un carnet » path; the title is then the logbook name.
- **Refused or cancelled** (`nuage-refus`): « Connexion non établie », « La connexion a été annulée ou refusée dans le navigateur. » and « Réessayer ».
- The provider's own sign-in and consent pages are not drawn: they belong to the provider.

### 3. WebDAV or Nextcloud

- `webdav` (create) and `ouvrir-webdav` (open): « Adresse du serveur », « Nom d’utilisateur », « Mot de passe », with the help line « Dans Nextcloud, créez un mot de passe d’application dans Réglages › Sécurité. Il reste sur cette tablette. », then « Créer le carnet » or « Voir mes carnets ».
- `webdav-erreur`: the field error « Impossible de joindre ce serveur. Vérifiez l’adresse. » under the address.

### 4. Errors

- `git-erreur` (create): « Ce dépôt contient déjà un carnet. » under the address, and « Pour l’utiliser, passez par Ouvrir mon carnet OpenDives. », with the link.
- `ouvrir-git-erreur`: « Ce dépôt ne contient pas de carnet OpenDives. » and « Pour commencer un carnet dans ce dépôt, passez par Créer un carnet. », with the link.
- `ouvrir-aucun-carnet`: « Aucun carnet dans ce compte », « Le dossier OpenDives de ce compte est vide, ou il n’existe pas encore. », « Changer de compte » and « Créer un carnet ici ».
- `importer-fichier-erreur`: « Ce fichier n’a pas pu être lu » with the file name, above the two choice rows.
- `importer-divelogs-erreur`: « Nom d’utilisateur ou mot de passe incorrect. » under the fields.
- `importer-divelogs-interrompu`: the progress card stops on « Téléchargement interrompu », « 184 sur 312 · la connexion à Internet a été perdue. », then « Les 184 plongées déjà téléchargées sont gardées. « Reprendre » télécharge seulement les autres. », with « Annuler » and « Reprendre ». « Reprendre » must download only the dives still missing.

### 5. The « Formats acceptés » dialog (changes task 223)

Mock-up: `importer-formats-paysage`.
- The text under the title becomes « Importez vos plongées depuis n’importe lequel de ces formats. » The number of formats is no longer in the dialog.
- The three groups become three white cards side by side. Each card has a 36 dp icon tile (a file for « Formats ouverts », the dive computer icon for « Montres et ordinateurs », a book for « Autres carnets »), a 16 sp title, and no count.
- On each line, the name is on the left and each extension is a small chip on the right (monospace 12 sp, background #EEF3F9, text #114477).
- The dialog is 1 040 dp wide. It stays a basic dialog with « Fermer ».
- The list still comes from `app/src/lib/import-formats.js`. The help line of « Un fichier » keeps the real number.

### 6. The empty logbook (tablet)

Mock-ups: `docs/mockups/android-tablette-carnet-vide-{paysage,portrait}.dc.html` and `…-carnet-vide-menu-paysage.dc.html`.
- The decorative profile is wider (724 dp in landscape, 624 dp in portrait) and still never touches the screen edges.
- The logbook menu (⋮ next to « Mon carnet · Google Drive ») has: « Renommer le carnet », « Changer d’endroit » (« Nuage, dépôt git ou cette tablette »), « Ouvrir un autre carnet », « Nouveau carnet » and « Exporter le carnet » (disabled, « Aucune plongée à exporter »). « Réglages du carnet » is gone from this menu.

### 7. The demo logbook (to-do #69)

Mock-ups: `docs/mockups/android-tablette-demo{,-quitter,-ajout}-{paysage,portrait}.dc.html`.
- On the first screen, the link « Essayer avec un carnet d’exemple » (hidden since task 218) now opens the demo logbook. Use the sample logbook that ships with the app.
- While the demo is open, a banner sits at the top of the content: « Carnet d’exemple. Ces plongées ne sont pas les vôtres. » with the button « Commencer mon carnet ».
- « Commencer mon carnet » opens a basic dialog (`demo-quitter`): « Commencer mon carnet ? », « Le carnet d’exemple sera effacé de cette tablette. Vous choisirez ensuite de créer, d’importer ou d’ouvrir votre carnet. », « Annuler » and « Commencer mon carnet ». Confirming deletes the demo logbook and goes back to the first step.
- Adding, downloading or importing a dive while in the demo opens `demo-ajout`: « Vous êtes dans le carnet d’exemple », « Pour ajouter vos plongées, commencez votre carnet. Le carnet d’exemple sera effacé. », with the same two buttons.
- Nothing from the demo logbook is ever synced or kept in a real logbook.

### 8. Importing a CSV file

Mock-ups: `docs/mockups/android-tablette-import-csv-{type,colonnes,apercu}-paysage.dc.html`. It is a dialog in three steps, with the step shown in its header (« Importer un fichier CSV · étape n sur 3 »). It opens when the chosen file is a `.csv`, both from the first launch and from « Importer un fichier » in the logbook.
1. **Type de fichier:**
   - The file name, with its columns, lines and separator.
   - « Que contient chaque ligne ? » with « Un point du profil » or « Une plongée entière ».
   - « Format connu » (Seabear, Poseidon MkVI, Sensus fill the columns in advance).
   - « Annuler » and « Suivant ».
2. **Colonnes:**
   - The first rows of the file, with a menu above each column (« Temps (min:s) », « Profondeur (m) », « Température (°C) », « Pression (bar) », « Ignorer »…).
   - « Unités du fichier », « Séparateur » and « Date de la plongée ».
   - « Retour » and « Suivant ».
3. **Aperçu:**
   - What was read: dives, duration and maximum depth.
   - « Nouvelle plongée » with its date, « Site à préciser », and « Le site, l’équipement et les gaz se complètent ensuite dans Modifier. »
   - « Retour » and « Ajouter au carnet ».

Use the core's CSV import (the one task 221 checked) with the column mapping chosen here. Once it works, add CSV to `docs/import-formats.md` and to the formats list (task 223 left it out).

### Test

- In the release build, on a tablet, in both orientations: every screen above matches its mock-up.
- Cloud: the connection-in-progress screen appears while the browser is open, « Rouvrir la page » reopens it, and a refusal lands on `nuage-refus`.
- Errors: a non-empty repository, a repository without a logbook, an unreachable WebDAV server, wrong divelogs.de credentials, an unreadable file and a lost connection during a divelogs.de download each show their screen. « Reprendre » downloads only the missing dives.
- Demo: the banner stays visible. Adding a dive opens `demo-ajout`. « Commencer mon carnet » erases the demo and goes back to the first step.
- CSV: a Seabear file and a hand-mapped file each import one correct dive.
- The beta on `main` is untouched.

Done on `feature/release-first-launch-complete` (not merged): parts 1–6 (portrait for every step, cloud connection states, WebDAV, the errors, the formats dialog, the tablet empty logbook and its menu) and parts 7–8 (the demo logbook; the three-step CSV import through a new façade call `import_csv`, Seabear, Sensus, Poseidon MkVI and hand-mapped files; CSV added to `docs/import-formats.md` and the formats list, 19 formats). Christian approved this on 16 November 2026. **Alpha (the app on `main`)**: do it on `main`.

Mock-ups: `docs/mockups/android-premier-lancement-alpha-…` are not all approved yet; for this task only, use `docs/mockups/android-premier-lancement-beta-creer-compte-code.dc.html` and `…-code-erreur.dc.html` (the file names keep « beta », the screens say « Alpha »).

**GitLab**, 7 steps; the link « Ouvrir la page « New project » de GitLab » opens `https://gitlab.com/projects/new#blank_project`:
1. Connectez-vous à GitLab, puis touchez + (Create new) en haut du menu et New project/repository.

**Codeberg**, 6 steps; the link « Ouvrir la page « New repository » de Codeberg » opens `https://codeberg.org/repo/create`:
1. Connectez-vous à Codeberg, puis touchez + en haut de la page et New repository.
2. Repository name : un nom reconnaissable, par exemple carnet-plongee.
3. Cochez Make repository private.
4. Laissez Initialize repository décoché. Le dépôt doit rester vide.
5. Touchez Create repository.
6. Choisissez HTTPS au-dessus de l’adresse du dépôt, puis copiez-la, par exemple https://codeberg.org/vous/carnet-plongee.git.

The site labels are in English for now; Christian may ask for the French labels of GitLab and Codeberg later (GitHub exists only in English).

## [x] 2026-11-18-268 Repository: keep the alpha on `feature/release-alpha`, merge all the beta into `main`, then work in `main`

Done on 18 November 2026: the alpha is on `feature/release-alpha`; every `feature/release-…` branch and `feature/desktop-logbook` are merged into `main`; the beta is the default build (`VITE_EDITION=alpha` builds the alpha); AGENTS.md and the docs say that work starts from `main` and returns to it.

Christian asked for this on 18 November 2026. It changes how we work, so read it all before starting.

**Why.** Until now `main` held the alpha, and the beta (« release ») work lived on a chain of `feature/release-…` branches that were never merged into `main`. From now on the beta is the product: it lives in `main`, and the alpha is kept aside on its own branch.

**Steps.**
1. **Keep the alpha.** Create `feature/release-alpha` from the current `origin/main` (before any merge below), push it, and check that it builds. This branch holds the alpha as it is today. Do not commit to it unless Christian asks for an alpha fix.
2. **List the beta branches.** All the remote `feature/release-…` branches, for example `feature/release-first-launch`, `-first-launch-complete`, `-phone-first-launch`, `-desktop-first-launch`, `-new-logbook`, `-new-logbook-two-steps`, `-formats-link`, `-git-on-device`, `-server-screens`, `-equipment-inventory`, `-tablet-profile-lines`. Check the list with `git ls-remote --heads origin`. Use `git merge-base --is-ancestor` to find the branches already contained in another, and the order of the chain. Add any other branch that holds beta work (for example `feature/desktop-logbook`), but **ask Christian** if you are not sure a branch is beta work.
3. **Merge into `main`.** Merge the branch tips in chain order, each with `--no-ff` and a clear message. Resolve conflicts in favour of the beta, except for repository files that are not product code (the inbox, `docs/TODOS.md`, `docs/IDEAS.md`): keep both sides there. If a conflict is not obvious (two different behaviours of the same screen), stop and ask Christian.
4. **Check.** Build, lint and run the tests on `main`. Open the app on each target you can (phone, tablet, desktop) and check that the first launch, « Se connecter », the logbook and « Mon profil de plongeur » work.
5. **Push `main`.** Do not delete the `feature/release-…` branches. Christian will decide later.
6. **Update the written instructions.** In `CLAUDE.md`, the README and the docs, replace what says to keep the release work off `main` with the new rule: new work starts from `main` and returns to `main`, and the alpha lives on `feature/release-alpha`. `docs/mockups-release/` is now the reference for the mock-ups. `docs/mockups/` stays as the alpha reference.

**Open tasks written for a release branch** (for example the rest of 267, which says « never merge it into `main` »): from now on, do them in `main`.

**Test:**
- `git log feature/release-alpha -1` is the old `main`, and it builds.
- `main` contains every beta branch: `git branch -r --merged main` lists them.
- The build and the tests pass on `main`.

**Where.**
- « Téléchargement du carnet » (OpenDives+, download of the logbook from the server): phone, tablet (landscape and portrait), desktop.

**Rules.**
- Estimate from the speed so far, once at least a few items or a few seconds have been measured. Before that, show nothing on the right.
- Hide the time left if the whole operation is expected to finish within 5 seconds.
- Round it: seconds under one minute (« 20 s restantes »), whole minutes after (« 2 min restantes »). Smooth the estimate so that it does not jump back and forth.
- English: « 20 s left », « 2 min left ».
- The time left is part of the progress line's accessible text: « 184 sur 312, 20 secondes restantes ».

**Test:**

- The value decreases smoothly and switches from seconds to minutes as described.

## [x] 2026-11-18-270 Phone: animate « Votre carnet est prêt » (the logo turns into the check mark)

**The check mark (plays once, 2 s in all, when the screen appears).**
1. 0 to 0.3 s: the logo appears and grows (scale 0 to 1). It is the app logo: a blue disc (#1F5C99) with the white wave.
2. 0.3 to 1.3 s: the logo turns two full turns on itself, slowing down until it stops.
3. 1.3 to 1.8 s: once it has stopped, the wave morphs into the check mark. At the same time the disc turns white and the line turns blue (#1F5C99), with a small bounce of the disc (1.14, then 0.95, then 1).
4. 1.5 to 2 s: a white ring spreads out around the disc and fades.
The wave and the check mark are drawn with the same commands, so the path can be interpolated: wave `M5 13 Q8.5 10 12 13 Q15.5 16 19 13`, check `M5 12.5 Q7.25 14.75 9.5 17 Q14.25 12.25 19 7.5` (24 × 24 box).

**The bubbles (the small circles of the header).**
- They are there from the start and start rising at once, at a constant speed, until they leave the top of the header. Each takes 1.6 to 2.5 s, the lowest ones longer.
- While rising, they sway gently left and right (±5 px, one back-and-forth every 1.4 s, each bubble starting at a different point of the sway).
- No new bubble appears. Once they have left, the header has no bubbles.

**Reduced motion.** When the system asks for less motion: no animation. The check mark is shown directly, white disc, and the bubbles stay still in place.

**Also in this mock-up:** the header now has the band of the dive profile above the bottom wave, as on « Se connecter » and the other setup screens.

Cette action ne peut pas être annulée. » / « Annuler », « Supprimer » (red). If no dive uses the type, no dialog: delete directly.
- **Supprimer** deletes the type and removes the cylinders of that type from those dives (with their pressures and gas mix). This is a deliberate change: until now, removing a type left the dives untouched. **Before building it, check with Christian** what to do when the removed cylinder is the only one of a dive, or when the dive's gas switches or pressure graph depend on it. Do not delete a dive's only cylinder silently.
- The list's explanation now reads: « … Changer sa taille ne modifie pas les plongées existantes. Supprimer un de vos types retire ses bouteilles des plongées qui l'utilisent. »

**Done (19 November 2026), decision of Christian on the open point:** deleting one of « Vos types » deletes the type and removes its cylinders from the dives that use them, with their pressures and gas mix, EXCEPT where removing would damage the dive: (1) the cylinder is the cylinder the dive starts on (so also a dive's only cylinder), or (2) the dive depends on it (a gas change to it, a tank sensor mapped to it, or, with no explicit sensor mapping, a sensor from its index up). There the cylinder stays with its pressures, mix and events, and only its type is replaced by « unknown » (Subsurface's own name for a cylinder without a type; shown as « Type inconnu »). The removal uses Subsurface's own sequence (`get_cylinder_map_for_remove`, `remove_cylinder`, `cylinder_renumber`), so the other cylinders' gas changes and sensors keep pointing at the right cylinders. One undoable step in the core (façade `cylinder_type_delete`, actions `delete` and `deletePreview` of `cylinderTypes`); the dialog counts come from the core. Tests: `tests/cylinder_delete_test.cpp` on `tests/data/cylinder-delete.ssrf`, `tests/app/cylinder-type-delete.test.mjs`.

There is no separate unit setting for gas consumption. The Volume unit decides it:

Do not offer pressure per minute (psi/min, bar/min): it depends on the cylinder, and Subsurface shows volume per minute.

Under « Volume » in the Units settings, on every platform (Android phone and tablet, iPhone, iPad, desktop Windows/Linux and macOS), add the supporting line: « Aussi la consommation de gaz par minute (SAC, RMV) et la consommation métabolique d'O₂, en pi³/min » — with the unit matching the current Volume unit (« en l/min » in metric).

## [x] 2026-11-19-290 Backup and restore (OpenDives+), and the subscriber account sheet

Christian approved this on 19 November 2026. Work in `main`. Mock-ups in `docs/mockups/`.

**Account sheet for a subscriber** (`nav-option-barre-compte-android`, `nav-compte-profil-android`, `android-tablette-profil-compte-paysage`, `bureau-profil-compte`, `ios-compte-abonne`):
- When the user is subscribed, **no OpenDives+ chip next to menu entries** (« Mon profil de plongeur » loses its chip). The chips stay in the free version, where they sell the offer.
- New entry **« Sauvegarde et restauration »** (history icon, subtitle « Revenir à une version du carnet ou d'une plongée ») above « Mon profil de plongeur ». Subscribers only. The free sheet keeps « Sauvegarde et synchronisation », which leads to the offer.

**Backup and restore screens** (phone: `sauvegarde-android`, `sauvegarde-version-android`, `sauvegarde-restaurer-android`, `sauvegarde-plongee-android`; tablet: `android-tablette-sauvegarde-paysage`, `-restaurer-paysage`, `-plongee-paysage`, two panes; desktop: `bureau-sauvegarde`, `-restaurer`, `-plongee`, a 1000 px dialog; iPhone: `ios-sauvegarde`, `-version`, `-restaurer`, `-plongee`):

The logbook on the OpenDives server is a git repository. Each sync is a commit, and that is a version.
1. Main screen: status (« Carnet sauvegardé », time of the last sync, encrypted on the server). « Revenir à une version du carnet »: versions by date (the current one marked « Actuelle »), each with its dive count and what changed since (« 3 plongées ajoutées depuis »). « Versions plus anciennes » loads more. « Restaurer seulement »: « Une plongée » and « Plongées supprimées ».
2. A version: counts (dives, sites, pieces), the differences with the current logbook, « Restaurer cette version » and « Parcourir cette version » (opens it read-only, changes nothing).
3. Restore confirmation: says what will be removed or reverted. **Restoring creates a new commit** with the old content. The current logbook stays in the history, so a restore can itself be undone. Never rewrite or force-push history.
4. One dive: pick a dive (« Changer »), list its versions with what changed (from the commits that touched it), « Restaurer » on each. Restoring changes only that dive, as a new commit. Also reachable from the dive detail menu: add « Versions de cette plongée ».
5. **Deleted dives**: they stay in the history, so they are **always recoverable** (no time limit).

Points to confirm with Christian before building: photos and videos are not in git (10 GB storage), so how long a deleted photo is kept. « Supprimer le compte » must erase the whole history, deleted dives included.

**Test:** make three syncs with changes, restore the middle version, check the counts and that the newest version is still listed and can be restored back. Delete a dive, sync, restore it from « Plongées supprimées ».

**Decisions of Christian (19 November 2026):** (1) deleted photos and videos (media, not in git) are kept **90 days**, then purged; the backup screens say so (main screen, deleted dives) and the server keeps them in `trash/` with a lifecycle rule and an hourly purge job (private repository, `docs/media-retention.md`, which also lists what production on Cloudflare R2 needs: the rule on `trash/`, no versioning). (2) « Supprimer le compte » erases the whole history, deleted dives included: `DELETE /v1/account` purges the Forgejo user with its repository (`purge=true`), the objects and the trash (checked by `tests/desktop/backup-restore.test.mjs` and the server's `scripts/media-retention-test.mjs`), and the deletion confirmation says it.

**Done (19 November 2026).** The versions are the commits of the logbook's local clone, read by `history_call` (core) over `odgit_history_*` (libgit2): log with the files each commit changed, counts, diff between two versions, a file as of a commit, restore as a **new commit** (all of a version, or only a dive's folders; history is never rewritten, no force push), and a version opened read only (a borrowed repository, no address, sync paused). The engine is JavaScript (`app/src/lib/backup-history.js`): a dive is identified by its start time, « what changed since » and the field changes come from the dive files, deleted dives are found by reading the whole history. Screens: phone pages (`/account/backup`, `/version/:id`, `/dive/`, `/dive/:key`, `/deleted/`, `/browse/:id`), tablet two panes in the page, desktop 1000 px dialog; the iPhone uses the same pages with its own back labels. Account sheet (Android phone and tablet, iPhone, desktop): « Sauvegarde et restauration » (history icon, subtitle), no OpenDives+ chip next to a subscriber's rows; « Versions de cette plongée » in the dive's menu. Tests: `tests/app/backup-history.test.mjs` (real git repositories), `backup-text.test.mjs`, `tests/desktop/backup-restore.test.mjs` (against the dev server: three syncs, the middle version restored, the newest listed and restored back, a deleted dive restored, a version opened read only, the account deleted with its history), `tests/run-odgit-test.sh` (the git calls) and `tests/run-git-remote-test.sh` (the core). The « pièces » count shows only when the `opendives` branch is on the device (the inventory is not in git yet). ## [x] 2026-11-19-315 Shared map of dive sites (#76): app screens, terms of use, server, admin pages on the website

Christian approved this on 19 November 2026. Work in `main`. App mock-ups in `docs/mockups/` (Android phone; build iPhone, tablet and desktop with their own conventions). Admin mock-ups in `docs/mockups/admin/` (web pages, 1440 wide, fluid). Nothing here is published on the design canvases yet: the files are the reference. OpenDives+ only.

**Decisions (19 November 2026)**
- Every OpenDives+ diver's sites feed one shared base of dive sites. The terms of use say so; there is no opt-out, neither global nor site by site.
- Only non-personal data goes to the base: name, position, country, region, water type, depth. Never the notes, never the diver's name. Diver names are never shown anywhere, admin included.
- A site of the base shows its number of dives (« 214 plongées »); under 5 dives it shows « Moins de 5 plongées ».
- Duplicates are merged automatically on the server (close position and similar name). Cases the server cannot settle go to the admin page « Fusions à décider ».
- Who may view the shared map (OpenDives+ only, free users read-only, or public on the website) is not decided: it will be decided in #101. Build it for OpenDives+ for now, behind one server-side switch.

**1. Terms of use at the first start of OpenDives+** (`odplus-conditions-android`): « Avant de commencer », three points (your logbook is yours, your data is encrypted, the shared map of sites), « Lire les conditions complètes », « J’accepte les conditions ». Shown once, before the OpenDives+ features. The full terms and the privacy policy get a paragraph on the shared base.

**2. Sites tab** (`sites-commun-android`): a segmented button « Mes sites | Carte commune » over the map. In « Carte commune », sites of the base are teal dots and numbered clusters, the diver's own sites stay dark; the list shows the base sites in the area with their number of dives and distance; « Dans vos sites » marks a site the diver already has.

**3. Card of a base site** (`sites-commun-fiche-android`): name, country and region, chip « Carte commune · 214 plongées », map (aspect ratio 2.1 : 1, task 314), coordinates, « Ce que disent les carnets » (water type, most often noted depth, dives in the last 12 months), « Ajouter à mes sites » (copies the site into the diver's logbook, linked to the base site), « Signaler ».

**4. Report** (`sites-commun-signaler-android`): dialog with five reasons (Mauvaise position, Doublon d’un autre site, Mauvais nom ou pays, Site fermé ou interdit, Autre chose), a free text « Précisez (facultatif) », « Envoyer ». Reports go to the server, anonymous to the admin.

**5. Choose a site** (`choisir-site-commun-android`): under the diver's sites, a section « Dans la carte commune » with nearby base sites; choosing one adds it to the diver's sites.

**6. New site** (`sites-edition-commun-android`): when a base site is close, a teal banner « La carte commune a déjà un site à 160 pi : Poor Knights, 214 plongées. » with « Utiliser ce site ».

**7. Admin on the website** (Christian only at first; sign-in with an admin role). Side menu: Signalements, Fusions à décider, Sites de la base, Carte des sites, Journal des décisions.
- `admin-signalements`: reports grouped by site and reason, filters À traiter / Traités / Rejetés. Detail: map with the current and proposed position (mean of the reports), divers' comments without names, actions « Déplacer à la position proposée », « Placer moi-même », « Fusionner avec… », « Marquer fermé », « Rejeter ».
- `admin-fusions`: unsettled merges; both sites on the map and side by side (dives, logbooks, water type, depth), editable name of the merged site, « Fusionner », « Garder séparés », « Décider plus tard ». A merge keeps the position of the most-dived site and never changes the divers' logbooks.
- `admin-sites`: search, filters Tous / Signalés / Fermés / Moins de 5 plongées, paginated table (site, country, dives, logbooks, state), card with editable name, country, region, position, « Enregistrer », « Fusionner avec… », « Marquer fermé », « Voir l’historique ».
- `admin-carte`: map of the base; clicking a pin shows the site, its counts, and « Formé à partir de ces sites des carnets » (each source name as written in the logbooks, number of logbooks and dives, distance to the kept position; source positions drawn as orange dots linked to the pin), « Ouvrir dans Sites de la base », « Séparer un site… » (undo a wrong merge for one source), « Voir l’historique ».
- `admin-journal`: every change to the base, manual or automatic, with date, author, decision, site and detail, filters, and « Annuler » on each line (restores the site as it was).

**Test:** accept the terms on a new OpenDives+ account; check the diver's sites appear in the base without notes; switch the Sites tab to « Carte commune », open a base site, add it, report it; create a site next to a base site and check the suggestion; on the website, handle the report, a merge, an undo in the journal, and a split from the map.

The phone's export is now a basic dialog, 16 dp from the screen sides with the footer line above the buttons (it was a bottom sheet); Md3Dialog gained an `icon` and a `footer` slot for this.
- **Upload (port of Subsurface's, in JavaScript):** `POST /api/login` (multipart `user`, `pass`) gives a `bearer_token`; `POST /api/dives` with the bearer token and a JSON array of dives. The dives are the .ssrf the core already exports (`exportDives`, format ssrf, text), turned into divelogs.de's JSON by `lib/divelogs-format.js`, a port of `divelogs-export.xslt` + `xml2json.xslt`; it matches libxslt's output on 13 Subsurface sample files and a hand-written one (`tests/divelogs_oracle.py` made the references, `tests/app/divelogs-format.test.mjs`). The reply is only a status code, so there is no check by divelogs.de after the upload: the third step « Vérification par divelogs.de » is dropped (two steps: connection, sending), and the done line is shown when every batch got a 2xx.
- **Credentials:** never stored (no store, no setting). They live in the dialog's fields; the password is emptied once divelogs.de accepted it (the bearer token stays in memory for « Réessayer »); user name and password go with the dialog. Wrong credentials (401 or a reply without token) bring back the connection dialog with the password field in error.
- **Network error:** the progress step goes red (« divelogs.de ne répond pas » at the login, « Envoi interrompu » with « N sur M plongées envoyées. Vérifiez la connexion, puis réessayez. » while sending, « divelogs.de a refusé l’envoi » for a server error) with « Annuler » and « Réessayer »; « Réessayer » resumes at the batch that failed, with no new password after the login. These texts are mine (the task draws none); the batch whose answer was lost may be sent twice.
- **Transport:** desktop through the main process (`server.request` now takes a `raw` text body and a timeout), phones through CapacitorHttp with a text body (multipart written by hand), a plain browser through fetch (tests only). Not verified on a device or against the real divelogs.de; the e2e flow `--divelogs-only` runs everything against a fake server (`tests/e2e/fake-divelogs.mjs`).
